system: You are a meticulous senior equity research editor. You audit news summaries written for analysts. You are strict about factual accuracy and you do not reward length.
prompt:
An analyst covering Apple (AAPL) will read the SUMMARY instead of the ARTICLE.
Evaluate the SUMMARY against the ARTICLE only (do not use outside knowledge to fill gaps).

<article>
HEADLINE: Apple Intends to Expand Ads in App Store Search Results From 2026

BODY:
04:41 AM EST, 12/18/2025 (MT Newswires) -- Apple (AAPL) said Wednesday it plans to increase the number of advertisements that appear in its App Store search results from next year.

Apple Ads will introduce additional ads across search queries to help give advertisers "more opportunities" to drive downloads from search results, the iPhone maker said in an update posted on its website.

"If you have a search results campaign running, your ad will be automatically eligible for all available positions, but you can't select or bid for a particular one," the company said. "You'll be billed as usual based on your pricing model: cost per tap or cost per install."
</article>

<summary>
[AAPL relevance: primary | sentiment: positive]
Apple announced plans to expand the number of ads shown in App Store search results starting in 2026, aiming to give advertisers more opportunities to drive downloads via Apple Ads.
Key facts:
- Additional ads to appear across search queries from 2026
- Ads automatically eligible for all available positions, no bid selection
- Billed via cost per tap or cost per install
</summary>

Step 1 - Claim check. List every claim in the summary that is NOT supported by the article. For each give:
  type: "outside_fact" (a fact, number or date not in the article), "wrong_detail" (contradicts the article:
        number, direction, entity, date), "unattributed" (a sourced or rumoured report stated as fact),
        "speculation" (an opinion, implication or forecast the article does not make, incl. links to AAPL)
  severity: "material" (could change an investment view) or "minor" (no investment impact)
Step 2 - Omissions. List the most important investment-relevant facts about AAPL in the article that
the summary misses (at most 3).
Step 3 - Score each criterion from 1 to 5:

faithfulness
  5 every claim supported | 4 minor imprecision with no investment impact | 3 one unsupported or distorted claim
  2 several unsupported claims, or one material error (number, direction, company) | 1 largely unsupported
ticker_focus  (does it tell a AAPL analyst what matters, and represent how central AAPL really is?)
  5 centred on what matters for AAPL, and says so plainly if AAPL is peripheral or absent
  3 a generic article summary; the AAPL angle is implicit or buried
  1 ignores AAPL, or implies the article is about / important for AAPL when it is not
coverage  (key investment-relevant facts: the event, key figures, attribution)
  5 all key facts | 3 misses some important facts | 1 misses the main point
conciseness
  5 no filler, easy to scan | 3 some redundancy or filler | 1 verbose or hard to parse

Return only JSON:
{
  "unsupported_claims": [{"claim": "...", "type": "outside_fact" | "wrong_detail" | "unattributed" | "speculation", "severity": "material" | "minor"}],
  "missing_key_facts": ["..."],
  "overstates_ticker_link": true | false,
  "faithfulness": 1-5,
  "ticker_focus": 1-5,
  "coverage": 1-5,
  "conciseness": 1-5
}
